summary: We created a role-playing game where every decision you make affects the well-being of the mission you are on. We took the role-playing game idea so that the kids who play our game can learn the importance of decisions on a space mission, but also have a good time while doing it, achieving the purpose of the challenge.
details: Our project works this way. At the beginning of the mission you will meet an astronaut named Nova, who will state the different challenges you face throughout the mission and will give you different options for how you will solve that problem. After you make your decision, the mission can be affected in 5 different aspects, which are: ship energy, life support, radiation shielding, food production, and communications. You will start with 100 points on each one and after you take the final decision you can either win points or lose them, if you reach 0 in any of these aspects you lose but if you make it to the end of the mission you win. The game helps players develop decision-making and critical-thinking skills, since every choice has consequences that affect the mission. Players learn about the key systems involved in space travel and understand how these systems are interconnected (a bad decision in one area can put the whole mission at risk). It also builds problem-solving skills and teaches players to weigh trade-offs, all while being entertaining. The intended impact is to teach kids and young players the importance of their decisions in a fun way by experiencing the consequences of their choices in a space mission setting. The goal is for players to finish the game having learned something valuable while also having enjoyed the experience. We built the entire game in Godot 4, using GDScript to handle the branching choices, the five-system point tracking, and the win/lose states. Combining storytelling with resource management turned abstract space concepts into something tangible and unpredictable, which keeps players wanting to try again even if they lose. During development, our main focus was keeping the mechanics easy to grasp while balancing the points so no single choice breaks the game, all while making sure the challenges felt realistic, educational, and clearly communicated on screen.
dataRefs: NASA Science, “Helio and You: The Moon as a Laboratory”
